items.title: Ray Drummond interviewed by Monk Rowe, Toronto, Canada, January 9, 2003
items.q: I’ve talked to my mother who retired as a middle school teacher... She says, “Raymond that’s the way it is,”

ctx.x: I am totally shocked. I had no idea that the level of intake — I mean these kids, they don’t know anything, I mean just compared to what it was — I mean just a rust belt, blue collar kid coming into a university had better speaking, writing, arithmetic skills, knew more about life, than any of these kids do. And now the best students are kind of similar to some of the best students, but it even becomes skewed with them because you can see certain little things that they don’t quite have that the best of the best…
Does it have anything to do with attention spans do you believe?
